item.title: RadianX promises solar-powered devices that never need charging
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Today’s portable devices are too hungry to run on traditional solar panels, but RadianX says its perovskite cells promise to make charging obsolete in some cases.

item.title: Box taps Nvidia’s Nemotron for new agent-first content retrieval system
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: The system can answer queries four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used.

item.title: A YC startup is putting $1M behind five unsolved materials science problems for AI
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Discovered Materials, a months-old YC startup that uses AI to find chip materials, is offering $200,000 for each solution to five open materials science problems.

item.title: Agility is the first pure humanoid robot company on the stock market. Are you buying?
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: Agility arrives on the Nasdaq today as the first publicly-traded pure-play humanoid robotics company.

item.title: Amazon ditches GrubHub, taps Uber Eats for Prime
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Amazon has made Uber Eats its official restaurant delivery partner for Prime members in the United States.

item.title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The company is said to be significantly dropping the amount it's spending on AI for its engineering teams.

item.title: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Data center opposition crossed party lines in Tuesday’s midterms.

item.title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: AI industry PACs spent millions influencing the 2026 midterms, with mixed results. Political groups are already looking toward the next election cycle.

item.title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.

item.title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: During its busiest week last quarter, Uber said only four people booked a ride using an AI agent.

item.title: Snapchat surpasses 30M paid subscribers
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The milestone comes a year after Snapchat announced a controversial limit on free storage for its Memories feature and informed users it would start requiring users to pay $1.99 per month for additional storage or subscribe to Snapchat+ to retain their Memories.

item.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.

item.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The startup allows software engineers to deploy teams of agents to work on various aspects of a project simultaneously.

item.title: Hackers stole DreamHost customer files and inboxes during months-long attack
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The web host said hackers exploited a vulnerability to access customer emails and files during a "deliberate attack."

item.title: Open source AI is booming. Hugging Face explains who profits.
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: Open source models are becoming more mainstream as enterprises, governments and startups alike rely on the promise of lower costs, more control, and more flexibility. But as increasingly capable models become more freely available, how do companies capture value? And with Chinese open models gaining ground, can American players keep up?  On this episode of […]

item.title: DuckDuckGo pitches itself to schools amid backlash over Google’s AI policy
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: DuckDuckGo is courting schools frustrated by Google's AI restrictions, pointing educators to its search engine and options to disable AI features.

item.title: Waymo confirms it’s shaking up its Uber relationship in January 2028
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The change will set up direct competition in those markets, as Uber has many other autonomous vehicle partners on its network.

item.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ is getting an outer space release and it hasn’t even come out in Europe yet
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: It is easier to watch the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything" in low Earth orbit than in London.

item.title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Sequoia is consolidating into a smaller, Bay Area–centered firm, shutting down the programs and offices it built during a 20-year expansion while announcing roughly $10 billion in new funds.

item.title: I tried Apple’s Siri Recaps. They’re surprisingly useful — and a little unsettling
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Apple's AI-powered Siri Recaps won me over in just one day, despite my privacy reservations. But there's still room for improvement.
